title: Hadrian's Wall
summary: Hadrian's Wall was a continuous Roman defensive barrier across northern Britain, running 73 miles (118 km) from Wallsend on the Tyne to Bowness on the Solway Firth. Begun after Emperor Hadrian visited Britain in 122, it controlled movement across the frontier and remained in use nearly until Roman rule ended in 410.

as_recorded.value: Emperor Hadrian (ruled 117–138 ce ) went to Britain in 122

where.modern_name: Hadrian's Wall, northern England (Wallsend to Bowness-on-Solway)

importance.justification: Major Roman frontier work and UNESCO World Heritage site, but regional in scope.

sources.title: Hadrian’s Wall | Roman History, England, UK | Britannica

reviewer_note: Sources differ on start (122 per Britannica; ca. 120-125 per Princeton) and on length (73 miles vs 80 Roman miles). End date is uncertain: Britannica says use continued nearly to 410, Princeton says held until 387 or a little later. The end year 410 is the end of Roman rule, not a precise abandonment date.
